You might start thinking, "What would the community say?" instead of "What does *my* heart say?" - **The "crutch" risk**: If you’ve *always* had this group to lean on, your brain might not practice the muscle of independent judgment. It’s like never walking alone because you’re always holding someone’s hand—you might feel unsteady when you finally have to step out on your own. - **The " sacred dependency" trap**: In religious contexts, this can feel especially charged. Judaism has always been about * " doing"* as much as * " believing"*— and " doing" requires * your* hands, * your* heart, * your* choices. The prayers you say every Shabbat aren’t just words; they’re a reminder that your relationship with the divine ( and with yourself) is deeply personal, even when shared.
